subject: Nordbridge: proactive p95 exemption / runbook requirements
messages:
From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@nordbridge.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.inference>
Cc: Nate O'Neil <nate.oneil@nordbridge.com>, procurement@nordbridge.com
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Request: 95th-pctl latency commitment for inference endpoints

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the integration looks promising. As we move internal approval forward, two asks popped up from our infra and procurement teams:

- They want a documented commitment for p95 inference latency for our primary route ("/v1/generate") during posted hours (8am–10pm PT). Target we discussed internally is sub-120ms p95 for 512-token avg requests.
- If that SLO isn't feasible without dedicated pooling, they need a clear fallback plan (model variant + routing) and a runbook for incident response and warm pools.

We attached our draft SLA language and a short list of production traffic characteristics. Can Redwood provide a carveout playbook and an indication of any uplift on pricing if we require a guaranteed p95 level?

Appreciate a pragmatic proposal — timelines are tight for our Q1 rollout.

Best,
Laura Chen
Head of Platform, Nordbridge Financial

Attachment: nordbridge-sla-proposal-v2.pdf (PDF, 92KB)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.inference>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.inference>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.inference>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.inference>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 12:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Request: 95th-pctl latency commitment for inference endpoints

Team — forwarding Nordbridge's ask. Quick summary: they want a documented p95 <= 120ms for /v1/generate during business hours with a runbook/fallback. They asked for impact to pricing.

Action items I see:
1) Eng (Karthik) — can we validate feasibility on hosted infra for their traffic profile and whether a sub-120ms p95 is achievable without Dedicated? If not, what model variant / routing policy would achieve it and what is the estimated cost uplift? Include assumptions (seq len, batching, KV cache hit rates).
2) Product (Marissa/Grace) — if we approve a carveout, we need to define the operational constraints in an SLA addendum and the runbook checklist: warm pool sizing, warm-start strategy, fallbacks, and notification windows.
3) CS/Ops (Sean/Monica) — draft the customer-facing runbook and incident postmortem expectations; procurement will need pricing delta.

Please reply with feasibility + timeline by Wed EOD (25th) so I can loop back to Nordbridge. If anyone needs data points (token distributions, historical p95 numbers), I can pull from console.

Thanks — Vivek
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.inference>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.inference>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.inference>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 10:47:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Nordbridge: feasibility check — p95 carveout

Quick engineering readout after a 1-hour perf pass and trace sampling against similar accounts:

- Baseline: hosted shared pool (no Dedicated) can hit ~160–200ms p95 for their supplied profile (512 tokens average, mixed prompt/template calls) under current batching behavior. That's above their 120ms target.
- With a warm-pool strategy + prefix/KV caching tuned for their workload, we can likely reach ~110–130ms p95 on smaller model variant (redwood-1-small) but that requires:
  * Guaranteed warm pool (min N GPUs reserved during 8am–10pm PT) OR a reserved burst policy to pre-warm instances on schedule.
  * Adjusted batching policy to reduce cross-customer batching for their routes (will increase unit cost).
  * A KV cache hit-rate target >= 60% for templated prompts; otherwise latency worsens.

Estimated uplift: 30–55% on token/throughput costs versus standard hosted depending on warm pool size and model selection. Dedicated pools drop variance but move to a reserved contract (we should present both options).

I can produce a sizing table (GPU counts, expected p95, cost delta) by Thu (26th) EOD if product wants to include it in the addendum. Also attaching a draft runbook skeleton covering warm pool triggers and fallback routing.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime

Attachment: nordbridge-runbook-draft.md (MD, 8KB)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.inference>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@nordbridge.com>, Nate O'Neil <nate.oneil@nordbridge.com>, procurement@nordbridge.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.inference>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.inference>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.inference>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.inference>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Nordbridge: proposal for p95 commitment and next steps

Hi Laura / Nate — thanks for the clear ask and the draft SLA. Internal alignment complete; here's a pragmatic proposal we think balances reliability and economics: 

1) Commitment: Redwood will guarantee p95 <= 125ms for /v1/generate during 08:00–22:00 PT for Nordbridge's production route with the following constraints (SLA addendum):
   - Traffic profile must remain within the supplied token and QPS envelope (we will define the 95th percentile QPS spike threshold).
   - Required KV cache hit-rate >= 60% for templated prompts; we will provide instrumentation checks.

2) Operational approach:
   - Option A (recommended): Dedicated reserved warm pool during business hours sized to Nordbridge traffic (estimated 2–3 GPUs initially). This yields most predictable p95 and lower variance.
   - Option B: Hosted carveout with scheduled warm instances + reduced cross-customer batching. Lower upfront commitment but higher per-unit cost.

3) Pricing uplift: Estimated 35% uplift on unit token / throughput compared to standard hosted for Option B; Option A moves to a reserved capacity contract (we'll provide a committed monthly rate). Final numbers and a sizing table attached.

4) Runbook & SLAs: Attached is the draft runbook (operational triggers, warm pool sizing checklist, fallback routing to redwood-1-small, notification windows). We'll finalize the addendum once you confirm Option A or B and sign the SLA change.

Next steps:
- Laura: confirm preferred option (A: Dedicated reserve OR B: hosted carveout) and attach procurement timeline.
- Nordbridge procurement: if Option A, share PO cadence so we can scope Dedicated onboarding.
- We'll update the addendum and circulate a final DocuSign link.

Marissa and Grace will follow up on the SLA language; Karthik will finalize the sizing table. Sean/Monica will own post-incident expectations and runbook refinement.

If acceptable, we'll schedule a 30-min alignment call this week to walk the runbook and talk calendar for warm-pool provisioning.

Thanks — Vivek
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

Attachments: nordbridge-sla-proposal-v2.pdf, nordbridge-runbook-draft.md
